title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 148
paragraphs: The spies, having thus observed everything and afterwards been released, returned to Europe. Meanwhile those Greeks who had sworn alliance against the Persian, after sending out the spies, next sent envoys to Argos. The Argives report that their own affairs happened like this. They were informed, they say, at the very first of the enterprise being set on foot by the barbarian against Greece; and upon being informed, and perceiving that the Greeks would try to get them as allies against the Persians, they sent messengers to consult the god at Delphi, asking how they should act to obtain the best outcome for themselves — since lately six thousand of them had been slain by the Lacedaemonians under Cleomenes son of Anaxandridas, and this was in fact why they sent to inquire. On consulting the oracle, the Pythia gave them this answer:
“You who are hated by your neighbors, but loved by the immortal gods — keep your spear within bounds, and sit well guarded behind it. Guard the head well, and the head shall save the limbs and body.”

Such, they say, was the Pythia's earlier reply to them. And afterwards, when the Greek messengers came, as I said, to Argos, they entered the council chamber and said what they had been charged to say. The Council's response was this: the Argives were ready to do as requested, on condition that they made peace with the Lacedaemonians for thirty years, and that they had half the leadership of the whole confederacy; and yet by strict right (they said) the whole leadership belonged to them, but it was enough to have half.
